scope: SBI Group's emerging JPYSC, Open Standard/OUSD, Startale, SMBC and BlackRock relationships; implications for XRP and Circle

observations.treasury_definition: Includes money-market funds comprised of T-bill ladders with less than three-month duration.
observations.quality: first-party issuer dashboard; monthly independent attestation reports stated, but only August 2026 attestation was listed on the page at capture
notes: Dashboard says page last updated Nov 4, 2026 00:00 UTC.
Supply and reserves are near $0.89B; this is much smaller than USDC but already material for a new stablecoin.
The dashboard states all Bridge-issued assets are backed 1:1 by short-term Treasuries and cash deposits.

observations.quality: first-party marketing page; internally inconsistent with Bridge's more recent reserve dashboard
notes: Marketing page says $468M in circulation and 54.9% cash/45.1% short-term Treasuries as of October 2026.
Bridge dashboard last updated Nov 4 00:00 UTC shows $888.33M supply and 13% cash/87% Treasury.

Marketing page simultaneously labels OUSD live and displays a future public launch event dated Nov 12, 2026; Stripe separately announced availability to Stripe businesses on Sep 30. Preserve the staged-launch ambiguity.
Businesses can mint and burn OUSD at no cost and become Open Standard partners.
Stripe says OUSD is created by Open Standard, founded by Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe and Visa.
Stripe products support OUSD for Treasury, Issuing, payouts, onramp and payments.

observations.metric: SBI and Startale Open Standard participation
notes: SBI and Startale joined Open Standard; the public partner list includes SBI Holdings, Coinbase, BlackRock, Visa, Mastercard and Stripe.
SBI and Startale are considering a proof of concept for interoperability between JPYSC and OUSD.
This is a network-membership and PoC relationship, not evidence of production JPYSC-OUSD flows or a direct bilateral Coinbase-SBI contract.
SBI and Startale signed a basic agreement with BlackRock entities to explore a digital asset ecosystem linking tokenized money-market funds and JPYSC.
No launch date, transaction volume or binding production commitment is stated in the release.

observations.metric: SMFG equity participation in SBI Startale Marketing
notes: SBI Holdings and SMBC Group signed a capital/business alliance to explore financial services using stablecoins.
SMBC Group agreed to acquire a 5% equity interest in SBI Startale Marketing, the SBI/Startale JV responsible for promoting JPYSC and developing use cases.
The amount invested and governance rights were not disclosed. This is not an investment in SBI Circle Holdings or Circle.

observations.source_type: SBI Shinsei Trust Bank/SBI VC Trade official release
notes: JPYSC outstanding approximately ¥20.1B as of Sep 7, 2026.
JPYSC Lending applications approximately ¥6.9B; applications are not necessarily funded loans or outstanding lending.
¥1B of trust assets was allocated to short-term Japanese government bonds.
The release describes total outstanding plus lending applications at about ¥27B; do not call that circulating supply.

observations.value: issued by SBI Shinsei Trust Bank; distributed by SBI VC Trade
notes: Initial service was limited to SBI VC Trade account balances; migration to public-chain distribution was planned after legal/tax practices were clarified.
Startale co-developed JPYSC.

observations.quality: announced investment contract; closing/payment not independently verified
notes: SBI said it would invest approximately $50M in Startale and make it an equity-method affiliate.
This is separate from the SBI-Circle JV, the Circle equity investment and the JPYSC reserve assets.
The release frames JPYSC as part of SBI's on-chain finance strategy; SMBC's 5% participation is in SBI Startale Marketing.
No evidence yet that SMBC will use XRP, USDC, RLUSD or OUSD in a production payment route.

relationship_edges.scope_note: OUSD is issued by Bridge for Open Standard.
Coinbase is one of five founding partners with Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe and Visa.
SBI joined with Startale; official partner page lists SBI Holdings. No direct SBI-Coinbase bilateral contract established.
SBI Startale Marketing is the SBI/Startale JV promoting JPYSC; amount and governance terms undisclosed.
Explore tokenized MMF and JPYSC ecosystem; not production.
JPYSC initially limited to SBI VC Trade account balances; public-chain migration contingent on legal/tax readiness.
SBI VC Trade is the distribution operator.
Open Standard says reserve income flows to partners less a management fee; free 1:1 issue/redeem.
OUSD is a new dollar stablecoin with shared reserve economics; no Circle participation in Open Standard was established in the official partner list reviewed.
SBI's JPYSC/OUSD/USDC/RLUSD network may be complementary or substitutive; production route-level evidence is required.

hypotheses.claim: SBI is building a multi-rail institutional network rather than backing a single stablecoin or blockchain.
supporting: SBI has relationships with Ripple/XRP and Circle/USDC/RLUSD; it is developing JPYSC with Startale, joining Open Standard/OUSD, exploring BlackRock tokenized-MMF links and bringing SMBC into SBI Startale Marketing.
disconfirming: The operating volumes and economics of each route are not publicly comparable; some are MOUs or account-internal products.
hypotheses.test: Measure issuer circulation, on-chain transfers, exchange volumes, route-level remittances and funded lending across each rail.

hypotheses.claim: JPYSC and OUSD could substitute for XRP as a bridge asset in some yen-dollar corridors.
supporting: SBI/Startale explicitly explore JPYSC-OUSD interoperability; OUSD is designed for global money movement and JPYSC is a yen settlement asset.
disconfirming: The interoperability is a proposed PoC, and SBI continues to support XRP through Ripple and SBI Remit.
hypotheses.test: Compare production corridor settlement asset shares and whether XRP bridge legs are retained or removed after any PoC launch.

hypotheses.claim: The stablecoin rails may complement XRP by providing fiat-denominated settlement while XRP remains a liquidity bridge or network asset.
supporting: SBI's portfolio contains both XRP and stablecoin products; a payment route may use different assets for funding, bridge, settlement and fees.
disconfirming: No public route-level evidence yet demonstrates joint use of XRP and JPYSC/OUSD in the same production flow.
hypotheses.test: Trace public route design and transaction-level asset paths where lawfully disclosed.

hypotheses.claim: Coinbase is hedging across stablecoin economics: it retains Circle USDC distribution economics while co-founding OUSD through Open Standard.
supporting: Coinbase is a founding partner of Open Standard and continues to report substantial USDC balances/economics; OUSD's model shares reserve income with partners.
disconfirming: No evidence yet that Coinbase has reduced USDC support or shifted its USDC holdings to OUSD; both can coexist.
hypotheses.test: Track Coinbase USDC distribution costs/revenue, OUSD balances, mint/redeem volumes, product defaults and customer holdings.

data_quality: Bridge reserve dashboard and OpenUSD marketing page disagree materially: $888.33M supply/$890.33M reserves at 2026-11-04 00:00 UTC versus $468M circulation and a different reserve mix on the marketing page. Do not average; the marketing page may be stale or use a different scope, but no explanation is supplied.

OpenUSD marketing page says OUSD is live and also displays a future 2026-11-12 public launch event; Stripe says business availability began 2026-09-30. Treat as staged availability with unresolved page inconsistency.
Bridge reserve dashboard lists only August 2026 as an available 2026 independent attestation at capture; the latest November snapshot is not yet independently attested on the page.
JPYSC lending applications are not funded loans; do not add them to circulating supply.
SBI/BlackRock and SBI/SMBC are MoU/capital-participation relationships; they are not production integrations.
SBI's $50M Startale investment was announced as an investment contract; completed payment/closing was not independently verified.
No official source reviewed established Circle as an Open Standard partner or Ripple as an official OUSD partner; secondary partner lists must not override official sources.
The >$1B founding-partner liquidity commitment is a reported forward commitment over coming months, not the current OUSD supply or proof that the full amount has been funded.

The Block reports Ripple among Open Standard launch participants, while the official OpenUSD selected-partner page does not list Ripple; retain as a secondary sourced claim pending primary confirmation.
CoinDesk CC reports Circle is not an Open Standard partner; the official selected-partner page also omits Circle, but neither source establishes a complete legal membership register.
next_actions: Reconcile Bridge's OUSD reserve/supply dashboard with OpenUSD's marketing metrics and obtain latest independent attestation.
Track OUSD supply by chain and transaction volume, especially Base and Tempo, against USDC/RLUSD.
Track JPYSC outstanding versus lending applications and any migration from SBI VC Trade internal balances to public chains.
Track JPYSC-OUSD interoperability PoC status and SBI/BlackRock tokenized-MMF integration.
Track SMBC's 5% SBI Startale Marketing investment amount and governance terms if disclosed.
Measure whether these rails replace, complement or coexist with XRP bridge use; no directional XRP forecast until route-level evidence exists.
Seek an official Open Standard partner roster or legal disclosure confirming Ripple and Circle membership status.
Reconcile the reported >$1B founder liquidity commitment with Bridge's live OUSD supply and actual funded balances by partner.

sourced_claims.claim: Ripple was among the launch participants/partners for Open Standard, according to The Block's June 30, 2026 report.
sourced_claims.corroboration: The official OpenUSD partner page's selected-partner list does not show Ripple; because the page is not an exhaustive roster, this is unresolved rather than a contradiction.

sourced_claims.claim: Circle is not a partner in Open Standard, according to CoinDesk CC's September 30, 2026 launch report.
sourced_claims.corroboration: The official OpenUSD selected-partner page does not list Circle; partner list is not stated to be exhaustive.
sourced_claims.confidence: sourced; official confirmation of absence not available

sourced_claims.claim: The five founding partners committed more than $1B to seed OUSD liquidity over the coming months; each reportedly received an equal initial equity stake.
sourced_claims.classification: reported commitment, not current funded supply
sourced_claims.confidence: secondary report; exact individual contributions and timing undisclosed
